question.text: The U - tube shown has a uniform cross-section. A liquid is filled in the two arms up to heights h1 and h2, and then the liquid is allowed to move. Neglect viscosity and surface tension. When the levels equalize in the two arms, the liquid will

Be moving with a velocity of <math> <mrow> <mfenced close=")" open="(" separators=","> <mrow> <msub> <mtext>h</mtext> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <mo>-</mo> <msub> <mtext>h</mtext> <mn>2</mn> </msub> </mrow> </mfenced> <msqrt> <mfrac> <mrow> <mtext>g</mtext> </mrow> <mrow> <mn>2</mn> <mfenced close=")" open="(" separators=","> <mrow> <msub> <mtext>h</mtext> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mtext>h</mtext> <mn>2</mn> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <mtext>h</mtext> </mrow> </mfenced> </mrow> </mfrac> </msqrt> </mrow> </math>
Exert a net force to the right on the tube.

solution.text:
When the levels equalize, the height of the liquid in each arm = h 1 + h 2 2

We may then visualize that a length h 1 - h 1 + h 2 2 = h 1 - h 2 2   of the liquid has been transferred from the left arm to the right arm.

Then, the mass of this liquid = h 1 - h 2 2 A ρ  

where, A = area of tube, ρ = density of the liquid

Distance through which it moves down = h 1 - h 2 2

∴    Loss in the gravitational potential energy = h 1 - h 2 2 2 A ρg

The mass of the entire liquid = h 1 + h 2 + h A ρ

If this moves with a velocity v, its kinetic energy = 1 2 h 1 + h 2 + h A ρ v 2

Equating energies, we get v=h1-h2g2h1+h2+h
